item.title: Knock Box (Seeking Greenlighting)
item.content:encoded:
The premise is pretty simple as it is a black box that when a user hears said knocking they are tempted to open it but they end up dead.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlighting: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Mysterious

Page Layout: Standard Format

Elevator Pitch: Imagine if you take a walk in the forest silent and you see a random black box just sitting there you feel no attraction to it until you hear it knock twice, your suddenly now just have to look at that box you don't know why you have to always look at it but it just feels like you should. Again the box knocks and this time you go to the box standing right next to you glee with excitement and you open the box a holy light shines through like a video game chest and… you dropped to the ground, the box closes and you die of a heart attack.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The black Box is a simple looking box or crate with a unknown brand stuck on the top it is a sticker on the left side of the box are other stickers saying "Every thing you would LOVE!" with pictures of a smiling family on it. The right side of the box reads "Are you having a rough time? containing in this very box you'll find the best things that will cheer you up!" although on the bottom of the box it reads in a black sticker "Silly you! this is the Bottom of the product!". After random increments of time the box begins knocking at the first 5 knocks the subject just simply examines the box, but after the 6th knock subject forcefully decide to open the box any attempts to stop said subject has always failed. subject that are going to open the box seem to not be affected by any sort of damage until said heart attack occurs. Subjects do indeed take physical damage but some how do not die until said heart attack. when subjects open the box or are about to there heart rate begins to rise and facial expressions begin to always show extreme excitement before open the box which there is a small chance that the pull out something out the box which at that point should be contained in a simple non see through bag. as soon as subject dies said box will close no matter what attempts of keep the box opened had failed. upon opening the box will show a bright yellowish light will glitter inside the box, the amount of objects in the box is unknown. objects inside the box seem to be quite simple man made objects of again unknown brand these objects include: pencils, blankets, coffee cups with coffee inside, toy cars, walkie-talkies, glass jars, gold bars, etc. each test of every subject pulls out a different object. it is presumed that the objects are what the subject wants or craves for.

Hook/Attention Grabber: The box is sure from its look it looks like a ordinary box but no matter the cause if someone hears that knock more than 6 times they always will get through what ever is in the way, (audio recording of the knock do not activate the reaction) the same effect happens with animals as well.

Additional Notes: None as of 12/1/2020


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. Also, please note the Ideas Critique required reading wordcount limit; your post is about 100 words over. Please address this before seeking further feedback. ~Zyn

item.title: Re: SCP idea- Leviathan of The midnight Sun (Mitternachtsonne)
item.content:encoded:
Hey there Anonymousauthor, I’ll be critting your idea today!
Note that I am not an official reviewer, so take what I say with a grain of salt. With that being said, let’s begin the crit!

+ Open Section-by-Section
Wooooosh

Elevator Pitch

So your SCP is some kind of large aquatic creature (nice physical description btw). However, I have much the same concerns as Captain Cold in regards to how the Foundation knows it’s appearance so well. Not only this, but why are they such problems associated with looking at it? Is it cognitohazardous? Also:

[…]located somewhere in the Atlantic at a Site known as The Ring.

I would have assumed you meant in or around the Ring of Fire, but that’s in the Pacific. So where is this Ring? And why was it constructed?

Central Narrative

You explain the abilities of this Leviathan in more detail here, where it mutates the surrounding sea life and makes them hostile. Unfortunately, this feels… very similar to SCP-3069, in that the anomaly mutates all surrounding sea life. Not only this, but like Angryman22 and Captain Cold I am concerned about this narrative, which seems to consist only of research missions ending in death. I’d recommend changing it.

Hook/Attention Grabber

Ok, but why can it alter the salinity around itself? This just seems like an extra ability tacked onto the anomaly in order to increase the pressure it puts on the Foundation.

+ Open General Thoughts
I don’t know about this

The idea is similar in ability to SCP-3069, the narrative is cliche and uninteresting, and the hook adds an extra ability randomly, making the whole thing feel a bit disjointed.

As an extra explanation for the narrative, explorations that end in death are completely fine (I actually have a soft spot for them myself). However, people usually expect some kind of twist, deeper narrative, or reveal in these exploration logs, so work on that.

I’d recommend three things:
1. Find something to seperate this concept from SCP-3069.
2. Work on your narrative! Brainstorm ideas, think of an emotion you want your readers to feel, and let that guide the direction your story takes.
3. Check out the Guide Hub for some great essays on ideation and story-ing!

And finally, to sum up your concept in one sentence1:
A large leviathan-like creature (presumably cognitohazardous) that mutates all the surrounding sea life and increases the salinity of the water surrounding it, with devastating effects on its environment.

Anyway, that’s it for my crit today. Thanks for reading, and I hope this helps!

Footnotes
1. This is to help you get an idea of the bare bones of what a critter sees when they read your summary. You may find something you don’t like here, or that we’re getting the wrong impression.

item.title: Re: Jetboat Sights and Adventures: Come Join the Extradimensional Fun!
item.content:encoded:
Hey Manhattan!

Got a bit of critique for you. First of all, I'll start with some of the more technical and grammatical issues.

+ show block
– hide block

"Observations have lead to believe that the clarity of the water is anomalouslyt obscrued from biological and mechanical vision." - It's anomalously obscured (minor spelling error). Also, you wouldn't say "biological and mechanical vision", the word vision is barely ever used when it comes to machines or items. Usually the word "detection" might be used. The whole sentence is really wonky to read. It jumps all over the place in terms of being very formal (like saying biological and mechanical vision) to being extremely informal (lead to believe). Also, saying "lead to believe" without a clear reference to who is being lead to believe sounds really wonky as well.

"Water from SCP-XXXX and Huka falls are chemically incompatible." Something being chemically incompatible means that they'll react if brought together (usually exothermically). Since I don't think that's the case here, a better term would be "insolvent", if you mean that they simply don't mix.

"Cross referencing has revealed that all fourteen unidentified species are related to avian, reptilic, and aquatic species." - You can't really "cross reference" when you're talking about animals. I even tried to look it up and found no reference to that term being used in conjunction with species.

Also, "avian, reptilic and aquatic species" is a really weird way to arrange species. Avian and Reptilian are both what is referred to as "animal classes", a subdivision of the Chordata phylum. There is no "aquatic" animal class. There's three classes of fish, one class of amphibians, and mammals which are occasionally aquatic. So you have one animal class listed, then another animal class, and then a vague term that covers potentially 5 animal classes.

Another thing that really irked me, that line basically described 6 out of the 7 animal classes under the Chordata phylum, pretty much all animals except mammals. But then in the story, there's a horned rat.. a mammal. So you give a description that includes 6 out of the 7 animal classes, and then in the story the animal is actually from that 7th. class not included.

"large increase of noise from human vocal cords." from the video log is also extremely wonky. First of all, you would say "increase IN", not increase of. Secondly, when transcribing a video log, you'd never use the term "noise from human vocal chords". You'd simply say "Shouting", "Screaming", "Chanting" or whatever else the people are doing. It's a much shorter word, and much more accurately describes the sounds being made. When you transcribe a video, your aim is always clarity and brevity. "Noise from human vocal chords" gives me virtually no information, especially compared to how much space it takes up.

If you want to aim for the more formal and scientific sounding tone, you really need a bit of research on the words you use.

Also, why isn't the Foundation keeping any kind of guard over these sites? What's preventing the Foundation from exploring them themselves?

About the story in general, I was a bit confused about who I'm rooting for here. Namid seems entirely passive and is quickly removed. Jack Bennett seems fairly aggressive and not entirely likeable from his monologues. I'm generally quite confused over what the real point of the story is. The SCP phenomena aren't really described in any kind of detail, and the people aren't either.

The premise itself could work, but the tone seems all wrong. The idea of a travelling agency that sells tickets to go to a number of SCPs that they've discovered, that could be a fun concept. The travel agency might be slightly clueless as to the exact nature of the SCPs, it could easily be a fun and light-hearted story.

When it's played straight, it doesn't really seem to work that well. The wondrous aspects are glossed over, and we're left with an angry man ranting on a boat.

item.title: Re: SCP idea- Leviathan of The midnight Sun (Mitternachtsonne)
item.content:encoded:
Requested by PM so lets see what I can do here for ya.

So looking at this SCP here, it seems almost overly complex. You describe what it looks like, but not how it does anything listed. Do the seven pupils serve a purpose or are they just there for aesthetic? And while most forms of saved images are ill advised, how do we know what the creature looks like with such detail from less than one minute viewings? I also am confused about the fauna transforming, did the SCP do that? If so, why did it do that and how? I would try and outline some more of these things so that reader has key information about the SCP rather than just what it looks like.

As for the narrative, I don't see much of one attached. I see you mention failed containment attempts, will they be apart of the article? The major thing I would try and tweak is it's discovery. Increased saltiness in the water? Concerning, yes. Foundation threat, no. Perhaps after initial NOAA investigation, there were reports of hostile fauna or the like thus triggering involvement. I am also rather bugged about the site you refer to as "the ring" I have no idea what this is, or why it holds significance. If you mean just another site, try Site-xxx. It's more formal and fits the article format better. Best of luck.

item.title: And another thing
item.content:encoded:
It's a -1 from me, but I want to add something to everything else that people have brought up.

I think this article's issues go farther than being tonal. To be frank, even ignoring the tone, it's just absurdly clunky to read. It's the use of punctuation more than anything. For example:

597 is to be hosed down weekly, with special care given to the areas around the nipples, to prevent the buildup of saliva and drool.

The second comma feels… just randomly there. It's an unnecessary slice in the middle of the sentence. There's no reason to put that beat there. It would feel like a harmless typo if nearly every sentence didn't have the same or similar issues. And listen, I'm not just here to be a stickler about proper punctuation. Honestly, breaking grammar to get a certain emotion across is a part of writing. A Franz Kafka story often has a lot of commas for a lot of long sentences. But in his stories, it meshes with the word choice. It's hard to describe, but I find the language used in a Kafka story (admittedly barring the fact that most of us have only read translations) works with the punctuation. Here, even though some sentences use clinical language, that language is at war with how they're cut up and organized. The word choice is (sometimes) clinical; the sentence structure is not.

The tone has been defended at times by explaining how this article is supposed to feature Foundation personnel becoming enraptured with this SCP. However, since this structure problem is present throughout the article as opposed to gradually shifting into disorganized madness, to me it feels like the article is unpolished. And when that's combined with some of these monolithic paragraphs, it makes me just want to stop reading. My eyes start to roll into the back of my head.

I'm sorry if this is coming across as harsh, and in all fairness I'm likely not a saint when it comes to this as well. But in honesty, it feels weird that in this discussion, the closest others have come to describing this issue is bringing up the tone problem, which for me doesn't quite hit the nail on the head (which perhaps also suggests that I'm the only one bothered by this, so… oh well). Not angry or disappointed in anyone, but seeing that just really made me want to talk about it. As such, I also think that if this is gonna stay up, it definitely needs a rewrite. I know it's Series 1, but personally, I think even by that standard it falls flat.

item.title: "The Gardener" [Seeking Greenlight]
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Split across multiple iterations of the document spanning across 10 years as containment procedures and behavior of the SCP object change.

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a humanoid who, by being near plant matter, accelerates their growth dramatically, and rather than bringing them into old age, makes matured plants into sentient "drones", dubbed SCP-XXXX-1, later -2 and -3, as the nature of the anomaly changes. While it begins as a child who turns plants into not terribly threatening sentient and hostile plants, later creations of SCP-XXXX display anomalous growths and sapience, making them more threatening. SCP-XXXX is not able to stop these events from happening, as it must be near living plants in order to live, and has no control of these creatures, often being prone to attack from them.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX is given its anomalous properties through the containment breach of a reality bender in a site near SCP-XXXX's home. A month after this breach, the Foundation investigates reports of deaths in a forest inhabited by SCP-XXXX, who had inadvertently converted several plants into SCP-XXXX-1 instances. An MTF unit is sent to find the source of these deaths, containing SCP-XXXX. Containment procedures begin simple, with only a modified humanoid containment chamber with a grass floor, as grass is found to be a non-issue when converted to SCP-XXXX-1. While SCP-XXXX grows over the span of a decade, containment procedures become more complex as it begins to generate SCP-XXXX-2 and -3 instances, eventually resulting either in the object's termination or a command to terminate it should it attempt to breach containment.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The main draw of the concept is SCP-XXXX-1+, and how their severity impacts the life and conditions of SCP-XXXX, who isn't really a catalyst for any events as much as its creations.

Additional Notes: My biggest concern is that sapient, hostile plant-monsters feels like a concept that's simply not threatening enough to warrant the drastic actions that I want the narrative to take. I've been toying around with different ideas on this matter, foremost being to make SCP-XXXX marginally stronger than a small group of people with sufficient plants nearby, and/or to slowly give SCP-XXXX plant-like qualities, causing its anomaly to take effect on itself, posing a security threat, but these are distateful to me both for fear of X-man syndrome, as well as the fact that the narrative simply isn't really that much about the humanoid. Any advice on this situation specifically would be greatly appreciated.

item.title: The Island of Lies (Seeking Greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP article

+ Elevator Pitch
- Hide
  • An island that will attempt to put any visitors to sleep. They will wake up on an identical island a ways away with some of their memories changed out. This can be anything from simple things like where they put their keys to aspects of their identity and personality itself.
  • People can go through this process an infinite number of times, further altering their memories and personality each time.
+ Central Narrative
- Hide

My goal with this is to focus on two subjects the Foundation has been using to test the SCP.

The first subject is a person who has been hit incredibly hard by the memory alterations, to the point where very few of his original memories still exist. This subject is being rehabilitated by Foundation staff in an attempt to see if he can be restored to his former self or if the changes are permanent.

The other subject is being used to test the effects of repeatedly sending the same person to the island. This subject also has barely any of his original memories remaining and has changed names at least three times, but rather than attempting to "fix" him, the researchers are simply layering on more and more changes to his brain. This part of the article would probably be more comedic in tone than the rest.

+ Hook/Attention Grabber and Additional Notes
- Hide

The big things I want people to be drawn to are the mystery of why and how the memory changes are being made as well as the stories of the two test subjects.

Additional Notes:
I want to know if the second island is really necessary, considering how small of a role it plays in the big picture. I was also playing around with the idea of the SCP being sentient and afraid of rising sea levels, let me know what you think of that idea.

item.title: Re: A Treasure Chest for (media) Pirates
item.content:encoded:
T.L. at your service!

+ Here lies crit crit
- Bye bye crit crit

I’m not too familiar with file sharing sites and FTP servers, and how sites usually obtain lost media, so I’m having a bit of a hard time seeing this as something too noticeably anomalous. I think you could try to accentuate more on its anomalous abilities because I’m certain that there are ways to regain some lost media via non-anomalous ways. Plus, if some of the lost media has no evidence for its existence, how would it have been discovered/obtained if it didn’t exist? Even if the lost media was obtained, how would people know that it is indeed lost media and not just something entirely made up?

Moving onto the central narrative, I don’t really find it uniquely interesting. All it’s pretty much about is global info breaches to which world governments and the Foundation collaborated to shut down sites containing confidential information. It doesn’t really go anywhere after that. Adding on, info breaches are a pretty commonly explored concept, so this idea has already been done many times. Plus, there’s not too big of a connection between this narrative and to what you have presented in the elevator pitch.

As for the hook/attention grabber, I think exploring the context within the archives might make for a better narrative rather than the narrative focusing solely on containment/handling of the info breach. However, I’m not sure about the part where the content from the archive mentally affects the researcher. I feel like it’s another one of those cliche tropes. If it’s an anomaly that can obtain all pieces of media, why not expand and try exploring other interesting content from within that archive and slowly build into the disturbing content? I think it will make the story flow a bit better.

Overall, there’s definitely some work that can be done on this. For now, try settling with accentuating the anomalous abilities to make it a bit more noticeable, and consider replacing the focus of the narrative onto the archive and the researcher exploring it.


If you have any questions regarding my critique, please let me know. You are welcome to PM me for another look, or you may follow up with someone from the Butterfly Squad Roster or IRC Chat rooms.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight ("The Boo Hag")
item.content:encoded:
Hello! I’m a long-time lurker and looking for critique on the concept for my first SCP. All feedback is welcome.

Seeking Greenlights: YES

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): Traditional SCP document layout.

Elevator Pitch: What is perceived as a horrid monster in Gullah culture/Carolinian folklore is, in reality, a caring mother. While not necessarily benevolent, this SCP does whatever it takes to care for its child.

Central Narrative:

+ Open
- Close

The narrative is intended to be told throughout the entire document, from the containment procedures, to the description, to a small collection of recovered documents and interviews. The SCP itself is what can be described as a “boo hag:” a skinless, humanoid entity that has the ability to disguise itself using victims’ skins, bewitch others using its voice, and transfer the life force it drains from victims to strengthen and heal other boo hags. Through the RD’s and interviews, the reader learns that the SCP and its daughter were hunted by humans; the latter was killed while the former escaped at the cost of losing her tongue. Having lost its daughter and ability to bewitch, the hag bides its time and waits for another chance to raise a child. Sometime later, the hag infiltrates a family under the guise of the patriarch’s late wife’s sister and cares for the patriarch's daughter, who is suffering from a terminal illness. The hag uses its powers to drain and transfer the life forces of local victims into her new daughter, but fails to keep her alive. The daughter expires, and the hag is apprehended by authorities following missing persons accounts. The Foundation intervenes and contains the hag; investigation of the daughter’s body reveals her to have been a young boo hag. The reader is left to decide whether or not the man’s late wife was also Boo Hag and to question the origins of the “Daughter Hag.”

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

+ Open
- Close
  • Explores a twist on the “murder monster” cliche and on a lesser known creature associated with Gullah culture and Carolinian folklore
  • The SCP builds up to a final reveal that will (hopefully) explain why the SCP is passive in containment (has no desire to lose another child), give a reason for the SCP to use its powers in the first place, why it infiltrated that certain family, and offer the right amount of ambiguity so as not to water down the intrigue of the SCP down with a concrete answer.

Additional Notes: I realize that choosing to write a humanoid SCP as my first article may be looked down upon, but I believe that I have what it takes to tell a compelling story.

item.title: The Dover Demon
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Comedy/History

Elevator Pitch: SCP-X is the creature known as The Dover Demon. SCP-X is a sapient small humanoid with bright white eyes lacking pupils, with a large skull and and no mouth, however it is able to speak, with its face moving as if it is speaking. It also has 4 long fingers. SCP-X is also able to become invisible, to hide itself from others. SCP-X is very friendly (and rather humorous) and likes interacting with trusted individuals. It typically walks on all four of its legs, but is capable of walking on its two hind legs. SCP-X has a high interest in floors, and anything on them, such as rugs, crumbs, shoes, and the shoes people are wearing.

+ Central Narrative
- Hide

The main focus of the article will be centered around an interview conducted with SCP-X shortly after its recovery. SCP-X is asked about where its from. This leads to a brief explanation that he was born in a cave, and that once he was around 19 he left his family and his cave, and started to explore the world. He then begins talking about how as he traveled, there was a lot of sounds: birds and mammals probably, but he was focused on the grassy fields and the smell of fresh soil.

He then goes on about how the fields eventually stopped, and he came to a place with big buildings and a bunch of people. And he goes on about how amazing these peoples shoes were, all black and shiny with neatly tied laces, and the ground was all neat and organized, with nice tiles. He then goes on about how he wandered around a bit, the buildings eventually got smaller, and eventually the ground stopped, and he was peering into a body of water. He wanted to keep going and see more shiny shoes, so he spotted a big ship nearby labeled "The Mayflower" and hopped on.

He says that the ground wasn't sturdy on the mayflower, and peoples shoes weren't shiny and laced, either. People wore old brown shoes with loose laces, and they often fell off of their feet. It was like this for a while, until eventually the boat stopped, and everyone started cheering. They all started getting off the boat on to a rock, and started setting up camps on the grassy fields.

The described that now that he was back on land, he could continue his journey on the neat paths. The problem was that there weren't any paths, just a lot of people in yucky shoes and grass. So he decided to stick around for a while.

Eventually, the people started organizing the ground, with rocks and stones. It wasn't as neat and clean as they were before, but it'd have to do. They still had dirty shoes though, which he didn't like. But eventually, people in red coats carrying long guns started appearing, and they had spectacular black shiny shoes. He started following them around, and learned a bit about them. They liked to push people in dirty shoes, "probably telling them to get new ones".

he explains that one time, there was a big group of people yelling at a bunch of the people with red coats and shiny shoes. Eventually, the red coated people started shooting at the people in the crowd, who started spilling blood all over the tidy ground. He didn't like the ground to be messy, so he left. But soon enough there was a lot of shooting and a lot of blood, which went on for a long time, until it all stopped and people finally started getting new shoes. The people in the red coats had left, probably because they didn't need to push people because of their shoes anymore.

SCP-X goes on to describe a few more brief details in his life, like how eventually big boxes with wheels started driving around on roads, and how shoes got more colorful, and eventually, he was caught by the SCP Foundation. The interview ends with SCP-X looking under the table, and asks the interviewer if he can try on his fancy shoes.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I think the attention grabber that the foundation literally has a little guy who was aboard the mayflower and was present at the Boston Massacre, but is just talking about everyone's shoes.

Additional Notes: I've always had some interest in the Dover Demon, and thought of this idea that might fit him. Give me your critiques and tell me what you think!

item.title: Re: "Long" Beach California (Seeking Feedback)
item.content:encoded:
Hey there BUCKSHOT74, I’ll be critting your idea today!
Note that I am not an official reviewer, so take what I say with a grain of salt. With that said, let’s begin the crit!

+ Open Section-by-Section
Woooooosh

Elevator Pitch

So it’s a beach 60 miles1 south of Long Beach where the water seems 80-90 yards2 away, yet never gets closer. To be honest, I’m not too keen on this idea (by itself). It isn’t very interesting in my opinion (all it is is a beach where the water doesn’t get closer), and seems to simply be the opposite of SCP-2684. However, if a good narrative is applied to it, it still could work.

Central Narrative

The narrative here consists of the Foundation sending out people to find out what’s up with the beach, and that’s about it. Some people die, they find some writing (which you proceed to not tell us about), and there’s a vague notion of a tall, mysterious entity that kills everyone who saw it. Personally, I don’t really like this. There isn’t any deeper narrative or explanation as to why the beach appeared, it just boils down to people being killed, which I find uninteresting.

Hook/Attention Grabber

The dry-drowning premise is unique[…]

Unfortunately, it isn’t. SCP-1812 is an excellent example of a dry-drowning premise that is in-theme, where we see the dry-drowning is due to the perceived higher gravitational pull on Earth’s water. In your idea, we don’t have an explanation as to why the first D-Class suddenly drowned, they just did. Oddly, they drowned at 8kms out rather than much sooner (which would make sense with the water depths of the average beach), and I’d like an explanation.

Also, as I explained earlier, the narrative is kind of boring, so the audio logs wouldn’t keep the reader entertained.

+ Open General Thoughts
I don’t know about this

The idea is (in my opinion) relatively boring, the narrative isn’t interesting and doesn’t give any explanation for the beach or entity, and the unique concept in your hook isn’t unique. Unless you overhaul the narrative to this, I don’t think your concept would survive on the mainsite.

Anyway, that’s it for my crit today. Thanks for reading, and I hope this helps!

Footnotes
1. Metric, not imperial, is the system used on the Site.
2. Metric.
